Selectivity specification

Source: R/0-build_selectivity.R
build_selectivity.Rd

Holds environmental linkages on selectivity parameters. An effect is written as a formula and composes additively with any Time_varying_sel process error on the same fleet, the two being separate mechanisms: a covariate effect against a deviation.

The linkages keys are the shape parameters of the parametric forms, so which apply depends on the fleet's Selectivity:

slp_asc, slp_desc

ascending / descending logistic slope (log scale); the double-normal widths, aliased sigma_asc / sigma_desc.

inf_asc, inf_desc

ascending / descending inflection age or length (natural scale); the double-normal peak and logit right-floor, aliased peak / right_floor.

coff

non-parametric selectivity-at-bin coefficients.

apical

a log-scale multiplier on one sex's whole curve, applied after the form and before normalization, so every estimated form takes it. See Details.

DoubleNormalSS3 (code 15) carries its own six under Stock Synthesis's names – dn_peak, top_logit, ascend_se, descend_se, start_logit, end_logit – and a linkage is the only way to vary that form over time, since Time_varying_sel is refused on it. A time block is ~ cut(Year, ...); annual deviations are a random-effect term.

Every parameter but apical takes link = "log" (multiplicative on the natural parameter) or link = "identity" (additive); apical is already a multiplier and takes "log" only.

Usage

build_selectivity(linkages = NULL)

Arguments

linkages

Optional named list of linkage_spec() objects keyed by selectivity parameter. Coefficients are per fleet by default (by = ~ fleet), except that fleets sharing a Selectivity_index estimate one parameter block and so take ONE coefficient for the whole group, which is what makes them mirror each other. Use linkage_spec()'s fleet argument to restrict a spec to particular fleets.

Value

A list of selectivity settings for fit_mod().

Details

The apical offset. Fishing mortality is one log_F per fleet and year shared by the sexes, and no form has a height parameter, so a sex difference in F can only come from selectivity. apical multiplies one sex's curve by exp(log_sel_apical) bin by bin, as Stock Synthesis's male-offset option does. Name the fleet and the sex that holds it (fleet = 3, sex = "male"; by defaults to ~ fleet + sex here) and the other sex is the reference. It equals the ratio of the sexes' peak heights only where their shapes peak equally, so for a sex-specific dome read it as the multiplier and take the peak ratio from fit$quantities$sel_at_age.

Only the contrast between sexes is identified, the common level being log_F, so one sex holds it and the fit is refused if both do, if no fleet or sex is named, if the species has one sex, on a Fixed, AR1 or Fleet_type = "Off" fleet, on a fleet sharing another's Selectivity_index, under link = "identity" (which could drive the multiplier negative), or where Sel_norm_scope = "WithinSex" would divide it straight back out. The contrast is informed only by joint composition (comp_data$Sex = 3); with single-sex compositions it rests on its prior, and fit_mod() warns when a fleet has neither. An intercept prior is on the multiplier's natural scale, so a lognormal() centred on 1 means no offset. See vignette("environmental-linkages-and-priors").

Priors on a selectivity parameter. An intercept-only formula (~ 1) with a priors entry puts a prior on the parameter itself, adding no year-to-year offset. Read it on the parameter's own scale: the slopes are log scale (lognormal()), the inflections natural scale (normal()). A prior targets one parameter, so in a two-sex model an unstratified ~ 1 prior constrains sex 1 only – use by = ~ sex. An init on a selectivity intercept has no effect, since the starting value comes from the data, and a prior on the double-normal right_floor is unsupported. Fleets sharing a Selectivity_index estimate one block, so place the prior on the group's lead fleet (its first that is not Off): a prior on a follower would penalize the shared block once per sharing fleet. On an Off fleet a prior is dropped with a warning and the fleet's linkage coefficients are held at their starting values, since the fleet has no data; on an Off member of a shared block it moves to the block's lead instead.

Like every selectivity linkage, a covariate acts in the hindcast years; projection years hold the last hindcast year's curve.

Examples

# \donttest{
# A cold-pool effect on the ascending inflection of a logistic fleet
build_selectivity(linkages = list(
  inf_asc = linkage_spec(~ cold_pool, by = ~ fleet)))
#> $linkages
#> $linkages$inf_asc
#> <Rceattle linkage spec>
#>   param:   inf_asc
#>   formula: ~cold_pool
#>   link:    log
#> 
#> 

# A normal prior on the ascending inflection (intercept-only formula)
build_selectivity(linkages = list(
  inf_asc = linkage_spec(~ 1, priors = list(`(Intercept)` = normal(0, 3)))))
#> $linkages
#> $linkages$inf_asc
#> <Rceattle linkage spec>
#>   param:   inf_asc
#>   formula: ~1
#>   prior:    (Intercept) ~ normal(0, 3)
#>   link:    log
#> 
#> 
# }
